newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hydro Magnesium says to expand Quebec plant.
newsitem.headline: Hydro Magnesium says to expand Quebec plant.

text.p: Hydro Magnesium, a Brussels-based division of Norway's Norsk Hydro, said on Wednesday it was expanding capacity its plant at Becancour, Quebec, to 86,000 metric tonnes from 43,000 metric tonnes.

The expansion would take place in two phases, it said in a statement. The first phase taking capacity to 68,000 tonnes would start in 2000, with construction of the second phase following once the first stage was operational.
"When fully in place the combined annual capacity of the Becancour operation and its sister plant at Porsgrunn in Norway will rise to 130,000 metric tonnes," it added.

The statement said the existing dehydration units would be modified to accomodate the first phase, and the project included new electrolytic capacity and technological improvements leading to higher productivity per cell.
Other changes would lead to reduced energy consumption, it added. Construction would begin in 1998.

"Important gains in efficiency and economies of scale will bring cost reductions considered essential if magnesium is to compete with steel, plastic and secondary aluminium for the light weighting of automobiles," it said.
The expansion was in line with the anticipated growth of the company's sales, it said.
